Hi Elena — great questions, and thanks again for the time. I pulled together quick answers below and attached a one-page pilot tier recommendation plus a short CSV with quant options we commonly propose. High-level first, then a short worked example invoice line at the bottom.

1) Pilot credit model
- Single unified credit balance: the pilot uses one credit bucket. Credits are consumed by token-equivalents; embeddings have different multipliers (see CSV) but you see one remaining balance in the Console.
- Streaming vs short chat: streaming consumption is per-token as usual; we meter tokens as they’re emitted (so streaming longer responses consumes more credits). Short chat messages (under 64 tokens out) are cheap — batching and prefix caching typically reduce cost further.

2) Quantization recommendations
- For T5 rerankers we recommend int8-calibrated quantization (Q8) as the default pilot profile. In our internal tests on reranking tasks we saw <1.5% delta in top-1 for most T5-medium variants and 20–35% throughput improvement on NVIDIA A10 / A100 family.
- If you need stricter fidelity, use a mixed profile (Q8 weights + float16 attention kernels). The attached quantization-options-summary.csv shows expected perf/delta ranges per family.

3) Caching and cold-start behavior
- Optimize supports two primary cache modes: prefix KV caching (stateful cache keyed by user prefix + model) and response-level result caching for deterministic calls.
- For your low-latency lookups we recommend prefix KV caching + small batching window (20–40ms). That gives sub-15ms median first-token in warm cache on our Dedicated capacity; cold-cache first-token depends on model size but we target <120ms on p4/a100-backed Dedicated SLA when batching is enabled.
- There is an option to reserve a small warm-provisioned buffer for keys you expect to hit during the business day — we can include that in the pilot for a modest additional monthly fee (line item below).

4) Packaging and mid-pilot top-ups
- Recommendation: Pilot Tier B (50k credit baseline / 6 weeks) with a 2x top-up option. If you hit >150% of baseline, top-up is automatic at the agreed unit price until you hit an admin stop.

Worked example (proposal invoice line items):
- Pilot Tier B (6 weeks): 50,000 Optimize credits — $7,500 (covers 50k credits baseline; includes 1 quant profile + 1 hour onboarding)
- Warm-provision buffer (optional): $1,200 (keeps hot KV set reserved during business hours)
- Additional credits: $0.15 per 1,000 credits (top-up rate)

Attachments: Optimize_Pilot_Tiers_v1.pdf (pilot tiers + SLAs), quantization-options-summary.csv (perf/accuracy deltas by family)

Next steps: if this looks good, I’ll loop Legal for a short SOW and Rishi can confirm an escalation credit in case of overage for the pilot. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if Procurement prefers.
